results.fact: Distance from Upper Duckabush camp/junction to Marmot Lake
results.correct_value: Marmot Lake is roughly 3.5 trail miles above the Upper Duckabush camp/junction (camp ~17.7 mi, lake ~21.3 mi from the trailhead)
results.evidence: A trip log puts the Upper Duckabush camp at 17.7 mi (2,700 ft) with the Marmot Lake/O'Neil Pass junction 0.1 mi beyond; Marmot Lake is widely given as 21.3 mi from the Duckabush trailhead. The itinerary's '~3 miles below the lake' is consistent with that; only the bivy card's '1.1 miles' disagrees, and bivy[] is owned by the camping clean-up, so no patch.

The only external ratings found call the Marmot Lake line class 1 (a peak encyclopedia entry and a climbing-site page it likely derives from, so effectively one source); no independent source rating it class 2 or 2-3 was found. Settling it needs a second independent trip report or guide rating the amphitheater-to-summit slopes.

results.correct_value: June: avalanche potential on the east-facing slopes below the summit while cornices/snow linger
results.evidence: hazards[1], best_season, watch_out[0] and approach_variants[0].hazards all state early-season avalanche potential on the east-facing slopes into late June; an external route page says to be aware of possible avalanche hazard on the east-facing slope while cornices persist until late June. Only the June cell of the avalanche panel reads N/A; the zone line (no NWAC forecast for this peak) is left alone.

patches.value: Possible on the east-facing slopes below the summit while cornices and snow linger

results.evidence: A trip report confirms Big Hump is about 1,000 ft up in ~30 switchbacks and 800 ft back down, so day 1's 200 ft loss (and day 5's 0 ft gain on the return over the Hump) is too low. But the itinerary day totals currently equal gain_ft 6200 / loss_ft 6400, and no source states a car-to-car loss/gain for this route, so the day figures cannot be changed without breaking the totals.

results.fact: Location of the Duckabush River ford
results.correct_value: The wide Duckabush River ford is above (beyond) Duckabush Camp, around mile 19
results.evidence: One trail page puts the ford of the Duckabush about 19 miles up the trail; a trip report places the 'upper river ford' between the Home Sweet Home junction (at Upper Duckabush camp) and Marmot Lake; a trip log puts Upper Duckabush camp at 17.7 mi, with only a log-bridged crossing just before camp. So descent_text and approach_variants ('above Duckabush Camp') are right and the approach's 'just before Duckabush Camp' is the stale copy.

results.fact: Where the climbers' creek turnoff leaves the trail
results.evidence: The approach says the turnoff is about 3 miles above Duckabush Camp (i.e. just below Marmot Lake at ~21.3 mi), while waypoints[2] (distMi 18.3), waypoints[5].note, approach_variants[0].notes and the itinerary place it ~3 miles below Marmot Lake near the camp junction. The primary route page that describes the creek turnoff could not be fetched (403) and no second source locating the turnoff was found.

The park's Royal Basin page says camp in designated sites only, listing Royal Creek, Lower Royal Meadow and Royal Lake. Two independent trip blogs say upper-basin camping is possible with a special permit issued directly by the Wilderness Information Center (not on the online booking site), on bare ground or gravel only; the park's reservations page does say sites not listed online are booked by phone. Sources conflict, and the only disagreeing fields are bivy[] (owned by the camping clean-up) and a waypoint type; settling it needs the WIC's current rule.

The row's own pins run west-southwest from the junction up Royal Creek, so 'east, then south' is wrong.
